facts.fact: 章首：今天又来了两位访客
facts.anchor: Two more visitors today. I think it’s going to snow again.

facts.fact: 枪管灰天空、尼古丁黄边缘，荒原是坟地般的白、像网球一样发亮
facts.anchor: The sky was a kind of gunmetal grey, with edges of nicotine-yellow. Beneath it the moor was sepulchrally white, and luminous as a tennis ball.

facts.fact: 两名警察站在门槛上问：Mr Sanderson？
facts.anchor: Two policemen were standing on the threshold. ‘Mr Sanderson?’

facts.fact: 他主动说「他杀了他的妻子」——用的是 ch36 路人的版本
facts.anchor: ‘He killed his wife. That’s what I heard. Anyway, I live here now.’

facts.fact: 警察的记录只有闯入者，没有谋杀案
facts.anchor: ‘It says here you made a report about a trespasser. Someone on your property behaving in a suspicious way. Nothing about any murder.’

facts.fact: 警察扫视外套、照片、家具、摆设——在找他精神失常的迹象
facts.anchor: He could feel them looking at everything – the coats on the back of the door, the pictures on the wall, the furniture, the ornaments – probably checking them all for signs that he was crazy.

facts.fact: 他失言说出「离婚之后」——把自己推成可疑独居者
他看出他们不信：亲戚，或许前妻——离婚后不稀奇
facts.anchor: He could tell they didn’t believe him. A relative. Perhaps an ex-wife. Not unusual, after a divorce.

facts.fact: 网球的刺眼绿色与警用背心、警车格子图案同色
facts.anchor: It was, after all, the same lurid shade as their police-issue jackets, the same colour as the chequered design on the side of their vehicle.

facts.fact: 警察定性：你大概是被恶作剧了
facts.anchor: ‘It sounds to me as if you’ve been the victim of a practical joke.’
‘Yes, I know what it sounds like,’ he said. ‘But I’ve been getting texts. Threatening texts.’

facts.fact: 敞开的箱子：网球、信件、照片、盒子，盒上用 Benn 的花体标着 Arthur Sanderson
facts.anchor: and the open chest with the tennis balls, and letters, and photographs, and the box, very clearly marked Arthur Sanderson in Dr Benn’s cursive hand.

facts.fact: 结尾他喊「我不是 Arthur Sanderson」——警察已经走了
facts.anchor: ‘I’m not Arthur Sanderson,’ he said, but the two men had already gone

facts.fact: 电塔如 Rombold 与 Wade 般无情地踏过落雪
facts.anchor: the pylon marched like Rombold and Wade, merciless, over the falling snow.
